## R315-P1 / R315-F001 CLOSED

reaper.rs:188-193 and :269-270 now use the same live_only filter for both
roster reads. Main's after-count explicitly filtered tombstoned rows out;
the new list(live()).len() counts the same fresh snapshot's live rows.
Dry-run still has one live list and before == after. Non-dry still refreshes
after from the database; it is not a subtraction from before. Candidate
eligibility, refreshes, guarded tombstones, retirement notices and receipts
otherwise have no delta. The merge retains both D-F258-3 and D-F258-4 and
both corresponding retro entries.

The real-store ListSpy regression proves all three calls across a dry run
and a real sweep are live_only: [true, true, true]. It excludes an already
retired row, reports dry (1,1) and sweep (1,0) with one reaped. Inspected L4
receipt restores the generic final read and fails precisely this assertion:
[true,true,false]. The existing live-index dispatch test establishes that
a live_only/no-pane list actually takes LIST_LIVE_SQL, not merely that the
flag was passed. No new mutation run was required in this read-only tree.

## Both reads priced

Observer: one live roster read per daemon per 600 ms (1.667/s). Reaper:
two live roster reads per non-dry sweep, every 5 seconds by default
(0.4 lists/s), not one read per seat. At T=3,279 and L=212, both roster
reads now traverse L index entries and materialize 2L=424 descriptors,
instead of 2T=6,558. Round 1 materialized L+T=3,491. Per-live-seat refreshes,
eligibility probes and candidate mutation costs remain; this is not a claim
that the entire reaper costs only its two roster reads.

Independent exact-SQL private-copy measurement (Python sqlite3 3.54.1,
30 warmups/300 paired samples, CPU median including tuple materialization):
observer 0.852 -> 0.360 ms; main's two full lists 12.759 ms; round 1's
live/full pair 6.789 ms; round 2's live/live pair 0.709 ms. The author's
12.43/6.57/0.71 ms figures are sums of separately timed query medians,
not a complete Rust sweep measurement; the independent pair run reproduces
the improvement and final 0.71 ms. Rows/order match. EXPLAIN walks seats_live
without a temporary sort; sqlite_stat1 says "212 1".

Command: nice -n 19 python3 <session>/files/pr315-r2-query-cost.py: PASS.
Raw result: <session>/files/pr315-r2-query-cost.json. The supplied live-table
copy was opened read-only; baseline/indexed variants were private in-memory
backups. Nothing wrote to the live store or modified the source copy.

No new loop, timer, poll rate, process launch or launch site. No per-tick/
per-seat launch cost is added. Index storage and maintenance are unchanged
from R1: insert on live registration/revival, delete on tombstone, and
delete/reinsert on live upserts assigning tombstoned_at even unchanged.
State/seq-only activity updates do not maintain this index. The prior
statement-only +0.34 us/upsert and +0.20 us/tombstone measurements remain
context; the author's committed tombstone/revive pair 0.72 -> 0.70 ms is
noise dominated by commit, not evidence that index writes are cheaper.
The PR's compact write-cost row still does not enumerate live upserts;
carry this existing R1 clarification, not a new final-round block.

The index is additive, not destructive, and introduces no retention policy.
Existing process/pane eligibility is unchanged; unknown evidence and pane
presence remain one-directional BRAKES, not a new ageing policy.
